about.title: Madera Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A defective product doesn't announce itself before it fails — a faulty part, a missing warning, a design flaw — and by the time someone in Madera realizes what happened, they're often already dealing with an injury and a mountain of questions. California's strict liability rules mean an injured person generally doesn't have to prove a manufacturer was careless, only that the product was defective and that the defect caused harm. That distinction matters, because it can open the door to claims against manufacturers, distributors, and retailers alike. If a defective product hurt you or someone you love in Madera or elsewhere in Madera County, holding onto the item itself — rather than discarding or repairing it — can matter a great deal to any later claim. LawProactive doesn't practice law; we simply connect injured people with an independent attorney, free of charge, so they can get clear answers about their situation.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: Not necessarily. Under California's strict liability approach, an injured person generally only needs to show the product was defective and that the defect caused the injury. This can make the path to a claim more direct than a typical negligence case.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Try to preserve it exactly as it was at the time of the injury, including any packaging or instructions. Don't attempt repairs or throw it away, since the product itself is often key evidence in a product liability claim.
